newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries idling at noon, short dates bid.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries idling at noon, short dates bid.

text.p: U.S. bonds were higher at noon, with the short end leading the way before a parade of major economic releases commences on Tuesday, analysts said.

Hedge funds reportedly continued to buy the three-year note after it closed so strongly last week, and the overall market tone remains firm after Treasuries withstood a sharp decline in the dollar overnight, experts said.
"There may have actually been some (bond) buying that was brought in on the weaker dollar," said Mike Strauss, chief economist at Sanwa Securities (USA) CO.

The bond market is discounting a weaker retail sales number on Tuesday, as well as tame inflation data later in the week, by trying to position itself slightly long and by getting long the curve as well, analysts said.

"As we approach what is expected to be very friendly data for the market ... we now have more views to the effect (The Federal Reserve) might leave rates on hold on the twentieth," said Lee Youngdahl, bond market analyst at Aubrey G. Lanston and Co. "So, all in all, that tends to boost the front end of market more than the long end."
